You might consider Vast Wealths instead of MotS. Of course, too many
master cards become a problem at some point.

> Thoughts:
> Well the idea about the deck is to make a Nergal vs. Nergal final in
> Storyline. Also how dose The Erciyes Fragments work can I take cards no
> matter where im placed from the Hell Princes deck?

Nope. You have to be his natural predator. For that, you have to
be fourth in order; that is, the guy who happens to be the predator
of the guy who is randomly chosen to go first. A 25%, completely
random, chance.

> And how dose it work
> with the timing on his "Tap to shuffel cards into his libary" cards?

I suppose you could tap it during your turn, when you have first option
to do stuff like that. Alternatively, I think you could just ask him
to declare whether he's using it at any given moment you would want to
use the Ericyes Fragment. If he says no, tap the Ericyes Fragment. It's
not like Magic. There are no "first-in-last-out" fast effects or
anything.

> Should there be Daring the Dawns in the deck?

Daring the Dawn works good with the action to Call the Great Beast,
obviously. I'm not sure how much else you'd use it for. If your
Nergal is in torpor with a Potence Card and the Soul Gem and it has
two or more blood, you can Minion Tap (if necessary) down to two
then attempt to leave torpor. If someone blocks you, Daring the
Dawn at inferior. That's the other obvious use. I can't think of
much else, although those two are important.

> Another Idea was to drop Soul Gem idea, but include Aigtas instead and
> then start to draw The Hell princes deck instead, making MY Nergal deck
> the bad one ;)

Again, you'd have to be Nergal's natural predator to make that work.

Fred

Nergal (normal promo) is only a promo card in teh Nergal pack for
storyline tournaments. He is legal for that tournament because every
player gets one, but AFAIK you can only use one of those promo
vampires. So the deck would not be usable for the storyline tournament.

Frank

I got the impression that you are not prohibited from using these
"storyline-only-promo" vampires in any way. The exception - that you
may add a copy to your deck - is only to make sure that even while
the cards are not yet tournament legal, you may still use at least one
copy of them. I don't think there is anything prohibiting you from
constructing a legal deck using the (now tournament legal) vampires
for a storyline tournament.

> Nergal (normal promo) is only a promo card in teh Nergal pack for
> storyline tournaments.

Once 30 days have passed from Nergal's release date - October 1st -
he is as legal as (for instance) Barbaro Lucchese.

Used to be, the Storyline tournaments only lasted a month. But
in their infinite wisdom (YEAaaaa!), White Wolf now has allowed
a longer one. So the promo cards released at the beginning will
at some point become completely legally to build into decks for
the same Storyline. (Of course, if it caused a problem, they
could always issue a special Storyline rule, banning the promo
in question.)

Fred
